messages:
marta: Heads-up — seeing a sustained spike of tiny GPU pods Pending in eu-west1 for ~12–18m. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/cluster/gpu-queue (last 30m).
ryan: link? which pool/az?
marta: eu-west1b warm-pool + on-demand burst. Mostly short-lived inference jobs requesting fractional GPUs (0.1–0.25). Lots of pods stuck in Pending -> PodScheduled -> AttachVolume.
alisha: can you paste a kubectl describe for one pending? suspect scheduler scoring + taints are leaving micro-gaps.
marta: sure — sample from job-id infer-ctx-42:

```
$ kubectl get pods -n inference | grep infer-ctx
infer-ctx-42   0/12 Pending   0     12m
...
$ kubectl describe pod infer-ctx-42
Events:
  Type    Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----    ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning FailedScheduling   12m   default-scheduler  0/30 nodes are available: 30 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
  Normal  Scheduled          11m   kubelet            Successfully assigned ...
  Warning FailedMount        11m   kubelet            AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume "nvdata" : rpc error: code = Unknown desc = attach timeout
```

marta: also seeing a bunch of small allocation fragments across racks (lots of 0.1/0.25 holes)
sre-bot: ALERT: pending_gpu_pods > 150 across eu-west1 in last 10m (threshold 50) :warning:
tim: nvlink/egress metrics show spikes on the same racks — there are packet drops and conntrack saturation during the autoscaler provisioning wave. Kubelet attach/attach-timeouts line up with egress bursts.
ryan: preliminary hypothesis: autoscaler spun up mixed GPU shapes (A100/RTX-like) to meet burst. Our fractional binpack doesn't coalesce across hetero-gpu shapes and taints get applied after provisioning, leaving micro-gaps that 0.1 pods can't fill. Pending pods queue but scheduler avoids preempt+repack because preempt window is too short.
alisha: proposing a short-term mitigation: enable soft-coalesce in scheduler for fractional requests (<=0.25) and extend preempt-window to 5m for eu-west1b warm-pool nodes. Also bump warm-pool drain delay to 2m so we don't constantly churn warmpool handoffs.
marta: I've started a canary on 3 nodes in eu-west1b, config diff pasted below. If it looks ok we'll roll to 30 nodes.

```
# scheduler-config (canary)
policies:
  - name: soft-coalesce
    fractional_threshold: 0.25
    allow_hetero_fill: true
preempt:
  window_seconds: 300
warmpool:
  drain_delay_seconds: 120
```

ryan: cost note: switching to larger homogeneous instances (fewer big GPUs) would reduce fragmentation but increases hourly cost ~12%. Sim simulated better utilization (+18% token/GPU). We'll need finance signoff for a permanent shape change.
alisha: I've opened PR #4829 with the scheduler plugin changes + a rollback playbook. If coalesce fix reduces Pending within 15m we keep; otherwise revert. PR includes metric alerts for preempt count, pending pods, and nvlink drops.
tim: I'll monitor nvlink and conntrack on the canary racks and validate attach success rates.
marta: running binpack-sim job 'microfill-sim-2026-03-21' to validate heuristics — job id sim-abc123. If sim looks good we'll fast-track.
ryan: SGTM. One more check: ensure KMS/HSM mounts not part of attach timeouts for these tiny jobs (small volumes mounting can block attach path). If so, we should use ephemeral tmpfs for these workloads.

alisha: action items in PR: 1) rollout soft-coalesce canary (3 nodes), 2) increase preempt window + warm-pool delay, 3) run sim job, 4) watch pending_gpu_pods < 30 for 20m and nvlink drops stable. Revert if preempt rate > 20/h.
marta: rolling canary now. ping me if you see reverts or new attach errors. :rocket:
